snippet.title: Can a 4th Division Player Win the Ballon d’Or? #shorts #eafc26
snippet.description:
In this FIFA experiment, I created a brand-new 99-rated player and sent him to Colchester City with one ridiculous goal: put up the craziest numbers possible and see if the game would still consider a fourth-division player for the biggest individual award in football.

The season turned into complete chaos. Between the league and the domestic cup competitions, we had almost 70 matches to get through, giving our player plenty of chances to prove himself.

By the end of the season, Colchester City had somehow completed an insane domestic treble, winning the league, the Carabao Cup, and the FA Cup.
He finished the season with an unbelievable 365 goals and 147 assists, completely destroying every competition he played in.

The only question left was whether any of that would actually matter to the Ballon d’Or system. Would the game ignore him because he was playing in the fourth division, or would those ridiculous numbers be enough to earn him a nomination?

We simulated all the way to the Ballon d’Or ceremony to find out.

Can a 99 rated player lead Colchester City to a Ballon d'Or in FC 26?

I put a custom superstar into the 4th division to see if they could carry the team to glory. Watch as I track every goal and assist on this wild journey to the top of world football.

snippet.title: How EA Slowly Ruined FIFA
snippet.description:
it's been almost 4 months but I'm back 
gonna try to be more consistent with videos but no promises




















-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FIFA sold over 325 million copies worldwide. It was the most played sports game on the planet for years. And today, longtime fans are walking away in droves — content creators who built entire careers on this game have quit, and even during TOTS, supposedly the biggest event of the year, the game feels completely dead.

In this video I go through the full story of how that happened — from FIFA International Soccer in 1993 all the way to FC 26. The birth of Ultimate Team in FIFA 09. The golden years of pack openings and Fut Draft. The slow abandonment of Career Mode and Pro Clubs. The broken metas that defined every single release. The introduction of PlayStyles and Evolutions, and how they completely destroyed the game's balance. And why, even with zero real competition in the football gaming space, EA still can't deliver a game that feels finished.

This isn't a video about hating FIFA. I've played this franchise since FIFA 9. It shaped a huge part of my childhood and it's still special to me — that's exactly why it hurts to watch what happened to it.

If you grew up playing Ultimate Team, Career Mode, or Pro Clubs, let me know in the comments which FIFA meant the most to you.

snippet.title: IS CRIMSON DESERT THE GAME OF THE YEAR #shorts
snippet.description:
This video highlights Crimson Desert, a potential contender for the title of one of the "best games" with its expansive "open world games" map and dynamic combat. Developed by "Pearl Abyss", it's one of the most anticipated "upcoming games" that promises an immersive experience. Watch the "trailerr to see why it's generating so much excitement among gamers.
Crimson Desert is about to drop and I genuinely think this might be the most ambitious open world game we've ever seen. We're talking a massive map packed with bosses, missions and secrets in every corner. You can explore it riding bears, dragons and horses. The combat lets you mix weapons, abilities and fighting styles however you want. And on top of all that, a story where your choices actually have consequences.
I know it sounds like a lot. But this game keeps convincing me every time I look at it. Could be the game of the year. Could be bigger than GTA 6. We'll see.
Drop your thoughts below — are you hyped or do you think this is just another overhyped release?
